notes: Labelled Lemme-clef, but its general validity is subsequently included in the conjecture4.15.9. Replace reversed indices only in the mathematical reading.

statement: If the key lemma holds for the monoid of injective quotient transitions, the colimit F(ξ) is isomorphic to one stage E, hence |F(ξ)|≤π₀.
notes: Units of the image monoid act as bijections, and all later transitions from a suitable stage are units.

statement: If there is no invertible tail for a left-cancellative monoid diagram, its regular-action diagram has injective transitions and arbitrarily late nonsurjective transitions.
repair: Left multiplication by a is bijective iff a is a unit: a right inverse is also a left inverse in a left-cancellative monoid.

statement: An I-diagram of sets with injective transitions and a nonsurjective transition beyond every stage, for I π₀⁺-directed, has colimit of cardinal greater than π₀.
notes: The extra source hypothesis |E_i|=π₀ is not used in the growth proof; this observation also handles applications with |M|<π₀.

statement: Under4.15.8.2, there is a strictly increasing chain (i_α) indexed by π₀⁺, beginning at the prescribed i₀, whose successor transitions are nonsurjective.
gap_or_error: The definition of I_α₀ prints β<α rather than β<α₀.
repair: Use the ordinal π₀⁺. At successor stages choose a nonsurjective transition; at limit stages choose an upper bound and then pass through a nonsurjective transition.

statement: The chain in4.15.8.3 can be chosen so that colim_β<α E_iβ→E_iα is nonsurjective at every α.
repair: At a nonzero limit α take a common upper stage for all earlier stages, then pass to a stage reached by a nonsurjective map; its image contains every earlier stage but is proper. At α=0 use E_i₀≠empty.
notes: Footnote187 is necessary for the proof as written at limit ordinals.

statement: The colimit of the selected chain injects into the original colimit and contains at least π₀⁺ distinct new elements.
gap_or_error: The edition prints E′_α where E′_∞ is meant.
repair: Choose ξ_α outside the image of all earlier stages; injectivity of all transition maps preserves distinctness.

statement: For fixed M and π₀, eventual invertibility for every π₀⁺-directed diagram is equivalent to nonexistence of a π₀⁺-indexed diagram all of whose strict transitions are nonunits.
gap_or_error: The defining cardinal inequality is printed |α₀|>α₀.
repair: Read |α₀|>π₀. If a tail of units never occurs, the previous transfinite construction gives a chain of nonunits; composition cannot turn a nonunit into a unit in a left-cancellative monoid.

statement: For Ind_π C, condition(a) says that every object is π-presentable in source terminology, equivalently every object is a retract of a representable.
notes: Modern presentability rank is π⁺. This equivalence of descriptions is independent of the conjectural assertion that all objects have the property.

statement: If C is idempotent complete, condition(a) is equivalent to essential constancy of all π⁺-filtered C-diagrams.
repair: A retract of a representable is representable precisely when the associated idempotent splits in C.

statement: Conditions(a) and(a″) are equivalent: every π⁺-filtered diagram admits a final poset presentation with constant object and one idempotent as every strict transition.
repair: Apply4.15.7.3 in the idempotent completion. Its objects arising as stages still lie in C, and their endomorphisms are unchanged; no splitting in C is asserted.
notes: The source hypothesis |C|≤π bounds the projector and morphism choices used in the reindexing.

statement: Condition(b) asserts literal identity of every sufficiently late transition in every diagram valued in a left-cancellative quotient of End_C(x).
gap_or_error: A nontrivial group gives diagrams naturally isomorphic to a constant diagram whose transition elements are never all identities on any tail.
repair: Replace identity by invertibility, or explicitly allow cofinal reindexing/trivialization. The worked C₂-valued diagram in the commentary is a counterexample.
notes: The PDF really prints =1. This is an edition/source error, not a transcription error.

statement: The reduction preceding4.15.9 is stated as using quotients of full endomorphism monoids.
gap_or_error: The actual construction on ms.455–456 uses a quotient of a submonoid, not necessarily a quotient of End_C(x).
repair: For a valid sufficient monoid criterion quantify over such subquotients; the strict-cardinal proof works uniformly for all of them. No equivalence for the printed restricted quotient quantifier is established here.
notes: This is a gap in the claimed reduction, separate from the literal-identity error.

statement: Condition(b′) excludes π⁺-long diagrams in the relevant left-cancellative monoids with all strict transitions noninvertible.
repair: Established for π>|C| by the source counting proof; the unrestricted boundary is not settled here.
notes: The equivalence between corrected eventual invertibility and exclusion of such chains is4.15.8.4.

statement: Theorem4.15.9 declares all of(a),(a′),(a″),(b),(b′) equivalent as printed.
gap_or_error: For C=BC₂, conditions(a),(a′),(a″),(b′) hold while literal(b) fails.
repair: Retain the verified equivalences among(a),(a′),(a″), and use the corrected subquotient monoid condition as a sufficient criterion. The strict bound is independently proved.
notes: The qualitative conclusion is not invalidated by this incorrect formulation.

statement: Grothendieck conjectures that Ind_π C is the idempotent completion whenever |C|≤π.
repair: Known from the proof here for π>|C|. A narrower improvement covers |C|≤π when all Hom sets have cardinal <π (π infinite), and the commentary also treats two-sided cancellative monoids. The full equality case is left unresolved by the checked literature.
references: Tendas2022Continuity, Lemmas2.5–2.6 and Corollary2.8; Lurie2009HTT, Corollary5.4.3.5
notes: This is not a claim that the general boundary remains a recognized open problem today; the report explicitly distinguishes failure to settle it here.

statement: Corollary4.15.10 says all printed equivalent conditions hold when π>|C|.
gap_or_error: Literal(b) is false even for a finite group and π=aleph₀.
repair: Its intended content(a),(a′),(a″) and(b′) is proved; read(b) with invertibility and the corrected monoid scope. The proof of the intended content is complete.
notes: Proof_status false follows FORMAT for an assertion false as written; it does not label the intended collapse theorem false.

statement: For a π⁺-chain of copies of a monoid M with injective nonsurjective strict transitions, |colim_i<α M_i|≥|α| for infinite α, and partial colimits embed into later ones.
repair: Successor stages contribute distinct new elements; injectivity prevents later identifications.
notes: The source writes the lower bound for all α; finite cases are harmless because nonbijective injective self-maps force M infinite.

statement: If |M|≤μ<π, a putative π⁺-chain of nonunit transitions yields μ⁺ distinct elements in a partial colimit which injects into a copy of M, a contradiction.
gap_or_error: The last displayed line replaces two valid inequalities by unjustified equalities.
repair: Use μ⁺≤|M_μ⁺|≤|M|≤μ. Both replacements preserve the contradiction.
notes: This proves the monoid statement uniformly for all subquotients of endomorphism monoids.

statement: If π exceeds the cardinality of a skeleton of C, Ind_π C equals its π-presentable subcategory and is an idempotent completion of C.
notes: Independent correct conclusion, after the preceding literal identity error is separated off.

statement: The source claims earlier applications of4.8.13 are thereby justified.
gap_or_error: The proof establishes a strict inequality, so an application using exactly the equality bound needs separate attention.
repair: Enlarge the cardinal where the application allows it; retain the equality-bound qualification for4.15.3 as stated.
notes: The audit does not silently transfer a proof across the boundary.

statement: For sets I,J with |I|,|J|>=2, the covariant double-dual functor E -> J^{I^E}, whose action is double precomposition, preserves no sufficiently large filtered-colimit class.
gap_or_error: No proof is supplied here; the variance of the power-set notation must be specified.
repair: The block at p464 proves failure at every regular rank by a functional distinguishing a constant function from all functions agreeing with it on a small subset.
notes: This is not the direct-image double power-set functor merely by notation.

statement: For I=J=2, the same functor has object function E -> P(P(E)) and is not accessible.
gap_or_error: The action on arrows is implicit.
repair: For u:E->F, an element Phi:2^E->2 is sent to (g -> Phi(g u)); the preceding proof applies.

statement: A replete full subcategory closed under retracts of an accessible category need not be accessible and accessibly embedded, even when described by existence of a map to a fixed object.
gap_or_error: The example uses a restriction on the ambient universe.
repair: The appendix proves this for commutative k-algebras with a k-point under its no-nonprincipal-|k|-complete-ultrafilter hypothesis; do not drop that hypothesis.

statement: M_z={x in M:Hom_M(x,z) is nonempty} is a replete sieve, hence is closed under retracts.
repair: If y->x->z, then y is in M_z; retract closure follows by composition.

statement: For every universe U there might be an infinite cardinal pi in U such that every ultrafilter on a U-small set selecting a cell of every partition into at most pi pieces is principal.
gap_or_error: This is an ambient-set-theory question, not an unconditional consequence of accessibility.
repair: Appendix commentary relates nonprincipal pi-ultrafilters to measurable cardinals above pi and explains the role of cofinal smaller universes.
notes: Open records the author's question; the modern conditional analysis is in the repair field and appendix blocks.

statement: Every suitably definable replete full subcategory of an accessible category closed under sufficiently filtered colimits is accessible and accessibly embedded.
gap_or_error: Definability is not defined, and the asserted implication fails under the appendix universe hypothesis.
repair: A cosieve of k-algebras without k-points is closed under every existing nonempty colimit but is not accessible. The author retracts the claim in footnote188.

statement: M'_z={x:Hom_M(x,z)=empty} is the complementary cosieve to M_z; these two full subcategories are accessible in M simultaneously.
gap_or_error: The equivalence is supplied later, rather than established at the point of the marginal annotation.
repair: Proposition4.16.7.8 and Corollary4.16.7.9 prove the equivalence; the block at p487 supplies the slice proof.

statement: For fixed z, failure of Hom(x,z) to be nonempty should be witnessed by a uniformly bounded member of a suitable presentable-object presentation of x.
gap_or_error: A uniform bound need not exist; the text's x_0 in the colimit clause is an index slip for x.
repair: Under the appendix hypothesis, reduced products modulo supports of cardinal at most pi give, for every pi>=|k|, a k-algebra with no k-point all of whose <=pi-sized subalgebras have k-points.

statement: For every infinite field k, one may take pi=|k| in the small-subalgebra obstruction criterion for absence of k-points.
gap_or_error: This sharper bound is false even without the appendix's universe hypothesis.
repair: The appendix exhibits k[x_i:i<|k|^+][(x_i-x_j)^{-1}:i<j], with no k-point but with a k-point on each subalgebra of cardinal <=|k|.
notes: The source here asks the more general eventual-bound question; this row isolates its suggested sharp form repeated in the appendix.

statement: If f:M->N^op preserves sufficiently filtered colimits and T is accessible in N and stable under the corresponding cofiltered limits in N, is f^{-1}(T) accessible in M?
gap_or_error: The printed stability hypothesis says N^op rather than the required stability of T in N; pi_1, N=Ens*, and I={empty} also slip in their notation.
repair: Even the intended stronger formulation fails under the appendix hypothesis: take f=Hom(-,k), N=Set and T={empty}; any nonempty inverse diagram of empty sets has empty limit.
notes: The source marks the question false in its later footnote.

statement: The retract-closed essential image of an accessible functor f:N->M need not be accessible and accessibly embedded in M.
gap_or_error: The printed ambient category N must be M.
repair: Use the accessible forgetful functor M/z->M, whose full essential image is the retract-closed sieve M_z.

statement: For accessible M and z in M, the slice M/z and its projection to M are accessible.
gap_or_error: The source labels the verification AQT.
repair: This is a comma/pseudopullback construction in accessible categories; one may also use presentations of maps to z. The infinity-categorical analogue is HTT5.4.6.7.

statement: S(pi) is the smallest replete full subcategory of M closed under L_pi-colimits and containing the essential image of f.
repair: It is the intersection of all such full subcategories. Rank conventions are explained in the opening commentary.

statement: The full L_pi-colimit closure S(pi) of the image of an accessible functor is accessible in M.
gap_or_error: The claim as stated does not impose a common strong accessibility rank.
repair: Proved here at every sufficiently large common strong rank kappa: S_kappa is Ind_kappa of the full subcategory on f(N_kappa), embedded using compactness in M. The arbitrary initially specified rank is not asserted.
notes: A good-rank theorem is distinguished from an assertion at every rank.

statement: The decreasing family S(pi) stabilizes for all sufficiently large pi.
gap_or_error: Closure under increasingly filtered colimits need not become constant.
repair: The block at p470 proves failure for the projection (k-Alg)/k -> k-Alg under the appendix universe hypothesis. A no-point object in one closure is excluded from a later closure by its own presentability.
references: Grothendieck1990XVIII, appendix Proposition4; root development p470

statement: If S(pi) stabilizes, its stable value is the least accessible and accessibly embedded full subcategory containing the image of f.
gap_or_error: This is conditional on the preceding existence and stationarity claims.
repair: At good strong ranks it follows from minimality of each filtered-colimit closure; the antecedent fails for the stated example.

statement: The same accessibility and eventual-stationarity claims should hold for the image of g^op:N^op->M when g:N->M^op preserves sufficiently filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: The conjunction fails: contravariant filtered-image closures need not stabilize.
repair: Under the appendix hypothesis take g:Set->CAlg_k^op, E |-> k^E, with |k|>=pi_0. A co-small reduced power belongs to S(pi) but is excluded at a later rank by presentability and the zero-algebra exception. The p470 development gives the complete proof.
references: Grothendieck1990XVIII, 4.16.3 and appendix Proposition4; contravariant development p470
notes: Accessibility of each individual contravariant closure is not settled here; stationarity is separately disproved.

statement: A category M admitting sufficiently filtered colimits and a small dense subcategory C of presentable objects embeds fully faithfully and accessibly in the presheaf category on C.
gap_or_error: Uniformity of the presentability rank of the small family C is needed; accessible here refers to colimit preservation, without assuming the source category accessible.
repair: Choose a common rank for all C-objects; the restricted Yoneda functor preserves that class of filtered colimits pointwise and is fully faithful by density.

statement: A full subcategory of a presheaf category closed under sufficiently filtered colimits automatically inherits a small dense subcategory of accessible objects.
gap_or_error: Ambient density does not descend to an arbitrary full subcategory; the source itself withdraws the inference in footnotes192-193.
repair: One must exhibit dense objects belonging to the subcategory. A nonaccessible cosieve supplies the source's obstruction; being a full subcategory alone supplies no such set.

statement: A category with a small dense family of presentable objects and sufficiently filtered colimits is accessible.
gap_or_error: The proposed contrary construction does not preserve the dense-family assumption, but the stronger assertion is also false under the appendix universe hypothesis.
repair: The p471 development embeds k-algebras by finite-free-algebra nerves in a presheaf category P, forms the nonaccessible no-map cosieve S, and adjoins the retracts T of representables. M=S union T has a small dense family of presentables and sufficiently filtered colimits, but accessibility of M would force accessibility of S.
notes: Open records the manuscript's treatment; the conditional counterexample is fully proved in the commentary.

statement: If M and M^op are accessible, then M is essentially small.
gap_or_error: Accessibility is not cocompleteness, and self-dual large accessible categories exist.
repair: Isbell's category of sets and partial bijections is self-dual and finitely accessible. The block at p472 constructs its filtered colimits and finite presentations explicitly.

statement: An accessible category with a small codense subcategory is essentially small.
gap_or_error: False for the same example.
repair: The one-object full subcategory on a two-element set is both dense and codense in the category of partial bijections.

statement: A locally small category with small dense and codense subcategories is essentially small.
gap_or_error: False even with a finite one-object dense and codense subcategory.
repair: The endomorphism monoid of the two-element set under partial bijections has seven elements and detects all partial bijections; the block proves fullness of the restricted nerve.

statement: For small I and accessible M, the full subcategory of M^{I^triangleright} consisting of colimit cocones is closed under sufficiently filtered pointwise colimits.
repair: Colimits commute with colimits whenever the indicated iterated colimits exist; at a large rank all pointwise filtered colimits exist.

statement: The subcategory of existing I-colimit cocones in an accessible M is accessible and accessibly embedded even if some I-diagrams have no colimit.
gap_or_error: The existence hypothesis in the familiar theorem cannot be omitted.
repair: Under the appendix universe hypothesis, the block at p473 constructs a finitely accessible collage E for which pushout cocones pull back to the nonaccessible cosieve of k-algebras without k-points.
references: Lurie2009HTT, Example5.4.7.9 (positive case only); root development p473

statement: If every I-diagram in M has a colimit, its category of colimit cocones is accessible and accessibly embedded in M^{I^triangleright}.
repair: Restriction identifies the colimit-cocone category with M^I; formation of colimits preserves sufficiently filtered colimits. HTT gives the higher-categorical analogue with the same existence hypothesis.

statement: Accessibility of the full category of pushout squares would imply accessibility of the full subcategory of epimorphisms in M^{[1]}.
gap_or_error: Requires the full replete accessible-subcategory meaning, not only abstract accessibility.
repair: Send u:A->B to the commutative square with top and left u and bottom and right id_B. It is a pushout iff u is epic. Pull back the full replete subcategory of pushouts along this accessible functor.

statement: A small cogenerating subcategory reduces the colimit-cocone question to the contravariant inverse-image question4.16.2.
gap_or_error: The meaning and strength of cogeneration must justify detection of universal cocones; moreover4.16.2 is false in general.
repair: This is not a proof of accessibility. The all-colimits positive theorem and explicit conditional counterexample are established separately.

statement: Proposition4.16.6.1: over a small Karoubian C, H plus accessibility and colimit preservation after the Q and Q' tests with nonidentity p imply accessibility of E and f:E->C.
gap_or_error: The source offers no written proof and doubts the restriction on p.
repair: The block at p474 proves the finite-test theorem: Q supplies universal colimits after splitting the stabilized base idempotent; Q' supplies presentability. Identity base idempotents are handled by H.

statement: Q is the category freely generated by a split idempotent xi --rho-> xi0 --sigma-> xi and one map xi0->eta; Q' is its opposite after relabelling.
gap_or_error: The isolated Q^op is printed in ordinary italic rather than calligraphic font.
repair: The generators and relations in the two diagrams give the announced five nonidentity arrows.

statement: Corollary4.16.6.2(a)<->(b): testing all strict pullbacks along small Karoubian categories is equivalent to testing Delta1,Q,Q', without restricting the image of p in the base.
gap_or_error: The unrestricted Q,Q' quantifiers are essential.
repair: Apply the finite-test theorem to each pullback over a small Karoubian C'; its local Q-tests may send a nonidentity idempotent of C' to an identity in C.

statement: Corollary4.16.6.2(b'): if C has no nonidentity idempotents, the Delta1-tests alone imply (a).
gap_or_error: Strict pullback can create an unsplit idempotent whose image in C is an identity.
repair: Take e->C selecting one object of the walking isomorphism. All Delta1-tests pass; pullback along the walking split idempotent gives the one-object nonsplit monoid {1,p}. Keep Q,Q' tests even when p maps to an identity.
notes: This is the assertion explicitly queried in source footnote196.

statement: For a Grothendieck fibration or opfibration, the unrestricted relative-accessibility tests imply accessible fibres and accessible reindexing functors.
repair: The Delta1 restrictions detect these conditions, using the gluing criteria of4.14.

statement: For a Grothendieck fibration or opfibration, accessible fibres and transition functors are equivalent to the Delta1-tests and to the tests over bases without nonidentity idempotents.
gap_or_error: The source's unrestricted b' fails for arbitrary functors but this structured case has isomorphism lifting.
repair: The proof supplied near4.15.6 establishes the total-category theorem for both orientations; such projections are isofibrations.

statement: Question4.16.6.4: do accessible fibres and transition functors of a fibration or opfibration imply accessibility after Q and Q' base change?
gap_or_error: The source leaves this unanswered.
repair: Yes. The explicit total-category proof near4.15.6 applies over every small Karoubian base, and survives pullback. The iso-lifting criterion in the root commentary explains the strict-pullback point.
references: Root and gluing commentary; PareRosicky2013, introduction

statement: A category accessible over a small base C is provisionally one satisfying the universal small-Karoubian-base-change condition.
gap_or_error: The printed reference to equivalent conditions of4.16.6.1 should refer to4.16.6.2; its proposed b' must be removed.
repair: Use condition(a) or the unrestricted condition(b). For small Karoubian C the commentary identifies this with accessibility of E and f plus isomorphism lifting.

statement: If E is accessible over small Karoubian C, then for every accessible M and accessible M->C, the strict pullback E x_C M and both projections are accessible.
gap_or_error: Strict and pseudo pullbacks cannot be interchanged without a reason.
repair: Proved in the commentary: the universal finite tests force f to be an isofibration, so its strict pullback is equivalent to an accessible iso-comma category.
references: BourkeLack2024, Examples4.8 and Remark4.9; root development p476

statement: The universal accessible-base-change property is proposed as the definition over a base C admitting sufficiently filtered colimits, without the original smallness restriction.
gap_or_error: The paragraph changes the displayed projection from the one to M to the one to E.
repair: We state both projections in the small-Karoubian theorem; a general nonsmall base is a separate definition, not a consequence of the proved finite-base assertion.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.1: a possibly large union of accessible cosieves of an accessible M is accessible in M iff it is already the union of a small subfamily.
gap_or_error: The printed premise omits pas and the union formula omits Ob on each summand.
repair: Choose a skeleton of presentable generators of the union, one member of the family containing each, and use closure of cosieves under nonempty colimits. Small unions are generated by the union of their small generating sets.

statement: For a monotone union indexed by an order directed beyond every U-small cardinal, accessibility is equivalent to stabilization at one index.
gap_or_error: The indexing order may be U-large; its directedness is externally interpreted.
repair: Bound the small subfamily of the preceding proposition by one index.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.2: for x in accessible M, the cosieve generated by x, consisting of y with Hom(x,y) nonempty, is accessible and accessibly embedded.
gap_or_error: The invocation of4.13 is not numbered fully.
repair: Choose a good rank making x presentable. The complement is closed under that class of filtered colimits; the canonical-slice proof of4.16.7.8 gives accessibility of both parts.

statement: Corollary4.16.7.3: a cosieve S in accessible M is accessible in M iff it is generated under outgoing arrows by a small set of objects.
repair: This is the small weakly initial set criterion for a cosieve, not generation by epimorphisms or a small dense subcategory.

statement: S is the increasing union of the cosieves generated by its U-small sets of objects, and S is accessible iff this union stabilizes.
gap_or_error: Must work externally with the U-large family of U-small subsets.
repair: Combine the previous criterion with a bound on a small union of U-small subsets.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.4: a nonaccessible cosieve exists in M iff there is a U-ordinal-length sequence x_alpha with Hom(x_beta,x_alpha)=empty for beta<alpha.
gap_or_error: The recursive inequalities use an external well order, not the arrow preorder; the claimed enumeration needs a skeleton of size at most the universe boundary.
repair: Pass to a skeleton via the dense presheaf embedding; recursively choose the least object outside the cosieve generated so far. The block at p483 supplies the complete size argument.

statement: Every sequence as in4.16.7.4 generates a nonaccessible cosieve, and every nonaccessible cosieve arises in this way.
gap_or_error: The proof's s_alpha as the least uncovered object should be x_alpha. One must enumerate isomorphism classes rather than arbitrarily many duplicate objects.
repair: The corrected least-uncovered recursion exhausts the chosen skeleton by the universe boundary; a small generating subset of the sequence would miss a later term.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.5: existence of a nonaccessible cosieve in some U-accessible category is equivalent to existence of such a no-forward-morphism sequence in a presheaf category on a U-small category.
gap_or_error: The presheaf variance and the symbol for the natural numbers have slips.
repair: Use the full restricted Yoneda embedding; full faithfulness preserves emptiness of hom sets. Covariant presheaves give the same existential assertion after replacing C by C^op.

statement: It is asked whether there is a U-ordinal-length family of fields with no morphisms from an earlier field to a later one.
gap_or_error: The k-algebra example alone does not answer the field restriction. The exact answer depends on the universe boundary.
repair: For U=V_kappa such a family exists iff kappa is not a Vopenka cardinal, with all external subsets of V_kappa allowed as families. The p485 development proves this using explicit Morleyization and graph coding followed by the fully faithful graph-to-field functor. Characteristic zero and no maps between any distinct indices are available in the negative-Vopenka case.
references: MillerPoonenSchoutensShlapentokh2018, Theorem1.1 and Remark5.1; BrookeTaylor2011Vopenka, Definitions1-3 and Proposition7
notes: In particular the sequence exists in the first inaccessible universe and is excluded in a Vopenka universe. This is a deduction supplied here, not a priority claim.

statement: A cosieve in any category is closed under every existing nonempty colimit of its objects.
gap_or_error: The empty colimit is correctly excluded.
repair: Choose any object of the nonempty diagram; its structure arrow puts the colimit in the cosieve.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.6: a replete sieve in accessible M is accessible and accessibly embedded iff it is closed under sufficiently filtered colimits; at a useful pi the same equivalence holds at pi.
gap_or_error: The final pronoun s'il is a grammatical slip only.
repair: For x in the sieve, every object of M_pi/x belongs to the sieve; the canonical presentation supplies generation. The converse is preservation by the inclusion.

statement: Corollary4.16.7.7: for an L_pi-closed sieve T and a pi-presentable-object presentation x=colim_i x_i, membership x in T is equivalent to membership of every x_i in T.
gap_or_error: The phrase pi comme indique above includes the sieve's L_pi-closure; without it the reverse implication is false.
repair: One direction follows from the structure arrows and the sieve condition; the other is precisely colimit closure.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.8(a)<->(a'): a cosieve S is pi-accessible in M iff it is generated as a cosieve by S intersect M_pi.
gap_or_error: Several slice-denominator omissions obscure the printed proof but do not invalidate the result.
repair: A nonempty cosieve in the pi-filtered slice M_pi/x is cofinal; use its canonical colimit presentation. All slice denominators are restored in commentary.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.8(a)<->(b): at a useful pi, a cosieve S is pi-accessible in M iff its complementary sieve T is.
repair: In M_pi/x, the cosieve S(pi)/x is cofinal iff it is nonempty; its complementary sieve is cofinal exactly when it is the whole slice. Apply the Ind-image criterion to both.

statement: Proposition4.16.7.8(b)<->(b'): the complementary sieve is pi-accessible iff it is L_pi-closed in M.
gap_or_error: The final printed reference4.6.7.6 should read4.16.7.6.

statement: Corollary4.16.7.9: a cosieve is accessible iff it is generated by a small set, iff its complementary sieve is accessible, iff that sieve is closed under sufficiently filtered colimits.
gap_or_error: Ranks must be enlarged to a common useful rank when comparing unranked assertions.
repair: Choose a common rank making the proposed small set of generators presentable, then use4.16.7.8.

statement: Corollary4.16.7.10: existence of a nonaccessible cosieve, existence of a nonaccessible sieve, and existence of a no-forward-morphism sequence are equivalent for accessible M.
gap_or_error: The example in footnote202 uses the first infinite Grothendieck universe.
repair: Combine4.16.7.4 and4.16.7.9. The appendix's explicit examples verify the conditional existence assertion.

statement: Lemma4.16.7.11: for a full S and useful pi, Ind_pi(S intersect M_pi)->M is fully faithful.
gap_or_error: S need not itself be closed under filtered colimits.

statement: A proper filter \Phi on E is a nonempty upward-closed subset of \mathcal P(E), closed under finite intersections and excluding \varnothing.

statement: For J\subseteq E put k_J=\prod_{\xi\in J}k_\xi, with restriction k_{J\prime}\to k_J when J\subseteq J\prime.
The reduced product k_\Phi is \operatorname{colim}_{J\in\Phi^{op}} k_J; \Phi^{op} is filtered.

statement: An inclusion of proper filters \Phi\subseteq\Psi induces a canonical k_\Phi\to k_\Psi, functorially in the filter.
